summary: The Model Context Protocol (MCP) ecosystem is the connective tissue between AI agents and real-world tools, exposing databases, browsers, design files, deployment platforms, and issue trackers through a single open standard. In 2026, adoption is driven by aggregator platforms that bundle thousands of integrations, gateways that secure and route MCP traffic for production, and a handful of individual servers that dominate daily developer use. This matters because MCP lets AI agents act reliably against live systems without bespoke glue code or credential leakage.
ecosystem_note: Aggregators bundle many MCP servers behind one managed endpoint and registry, gateways proxy/secure/route MCP traffic for governance and auth, and individual servers connect an agent to one specific tool or capability.

tools.name: Playwright MCP
tools.connects_to: Browser automation across Chrome, Firefox, and WebKit via 25+ tools using accessibility-tree snapshots (no vision models or screenshots required)
strengths: Most-used MCP server in the community by public usage rankings
Fast, LLM-friendly structured APIs without screenshot processing
Runs in CI/CD environments like GitHub Actions
tools.best_for: Reliable AI-driven browser testing and web automation without writing Playwright code

tools.name: GitHub MCP Server
tools.connects_to: GitHub repositories, issues, pull requests, Actions, and code search via an OAuth-secured remote MCP endpoint
tools.pricing_paid: Free with GitHub account; usage tied to GitHub plans
strengths: Official OAuth-secured remote server (no local install)
Ubiquitous across coding agents (Cursor, Claude Code, Codex)
Top pick for repo triage and automation workflows
tools.best_for: AI agents performing code review, issue triage, and repository automation

tools.name: Composio
tools.connects_to: A managed endpoint exposing 1,500+ apps (Slack, GitHub, databases, Playwright, and more) with built-in auth and a self-learning tool-selection layer
tools.pricing_paid: Free open-source core; usage-based enterprise plans
strengths: 1B+ tool calls run on the platform
Self-learning layer improves tool selection and token efficiency (30% more accurate on 2x fewer tokens for repeat tasks)
CLI to add tools and auth to coding agents
tools.best_for: Teams building production agents that need many pre-authenticated integrations through one endpoint

tools.name: Context7
tools.connects_to: Up-to-date, version-specific library documentation and code examples injected directly into agent context
tools.pricing_paid: Free tier; paid usage via Upstash plans
strengths: Consistently a top pick across Cursor, Claude Code, and Codex
Simple drop-in for any coding agent
tools.best_for: Giving coding agents accurate, current documentation for the libraries they generate code against

tools.name: Smithery
tools.connects_to: A large registry/marketplace of MCP servers for discovery, configuration, and installation into agents
strengths: One of the largest MCP server registries for discovery
Central hub referenced across the ecosystem
tools.best_for: Discovering and installing community MCP servers into coding agents

tools.name: Cloudflare MCP
tools.connects_to: Remote MCP server hosting and gateway/proxy with OAuth, deployed on Cloudflare Workers for secured, scalable endpoints
tools.pricing_paid: Free tier via Workers; paid Workers/enterprise plans
strengths: First-class remote MCP hosting on the edge
Eliminates local install and credential leakage
tools.best_for: Shipping production-grade hosted/remote MCP servers with built-in auth

tools.name: Figma MCP
tools.connects_to: Figma design files, frames, and components so agents can read designs and generate matching code
tools.pricing_paid: Free with Figma account; usage tied to Figma plans
tools.best_for: Generating accurate UI code directly from Figma designs with AI agents

tools.name: Glama
tools.connects_to: A hosted registry that runs MCP servers for you with gateway access, rather than requiring self-hosting
strengths: Hosts and runs MCP servers on your behalf
tools.best_for: Developers who want managed, hosted MCP servers without running infrastructure

tools.name: n8n MCP
tools.connects_to: n8n workflow automation, letting agents trigger and build automations across 400+ app integrations
strengths: Bridges AI agents with mature workflow automation
Huge library of existing app integrations
tools.best_for: Connecting AI agents to multi-step automation workflows across many apps

tools.name: Docker MCP
tools.connects_to: Containerized MCP servers via the Docker MCP Catalog and Toolkit for secure, isolated tool execution
tools.pricing_paid: Free with Docker Desktop; paid Docker Business/Team plans
strengths: Secure, sandboxed MCP server execution in containers
Curated MCP Catalog of verified servers
Consistent environments across machines and CI
tools.best_for: Running MCP servers in isolated, reproducible containers for security and portability

tools.name: Supabase MCP
tools.connects_to: Supabase Postgres databases, auth, and storage so agents can query and manage backend data
tools.pricing_paid: Free tier; paid Supabase Pro/Team plans
tools.best_for: Letting AI agents query and manage Postgres-backed application data

tools.name: Notion MCP
tools.connects_to: Notion pages, databases, and workspace content for reading and writing knowledge-base data
tools.pricing_paid: Free with Notion account; paid Notion plans
strengths: Connects agents to team knowledge bases
Widely used for docs and task automation
tools.best_for: AI agents reading and updating Notion-based documentation and project data
